tagline: Find any audit result — any check, on any asset — in one search.
problem: Compliance scans leave one result per check per asset — tens of thousands of rows. "Which hosts fail this control?", "what does this audit file say about that server?" and "everything failing PCI" are simple questions that shouldn't need a dashboard or SQL.
does: Explorer › Compliance searches every audit result in navi.db by check name or ID, audit file, framework, status, or asset — hostname, IP or UUID — with failed results first. Each row opens to show actual vs expected, the fix, and the framework references; a check opens across every asset that ran it.

glance.caption: Explorer › Compliance's headline numbers on a 128-asset lab, counted over the whole search: 660 audit results on 60 assets across 11 checks, a 54.2% pass rate, 275 failed, 60 warnings — and all 60 assets failing at least one check.

capabilities: check name or ID, audit file, hostname, IP or asset UUID in one box.
by status (failed, warning, passed, other), audit file and framework, with result counts in each list.
results, assets, checks, pass rate, failed, warnings and assets failing a check — counted over every match, not just the page.
actual vs expected, the solution, check info, a reference link, and the framework controls it maps to.
click a check ID to see it on every asset that ran it.
each asset opens Asset Dossier, or Compliance Drill-down for every check on that asset.
a question becomes one read-only SQL query over the audit-result table that you can edit before it runs (needs an AI model).
export the whole search (every row — a background export job past 5,000) or send it through Notify & Report.
how: Explorer › Compliance runs read-only searches over the compliance table in your local navi.db (filled by `navi config update compliance`), joined to assets for hostname and IP. Results page on the server, 20 rows a page (up to 50), so it stays fast on large estates.
who: Auditors and GRC analysts answering a specific question, and system owners checking how their hosts measure against a benchmark.
better: Compliance Overview gives the estate-wide verdict, Compliance Drill-down explains one asset, and Audit Authoring writes the custom checks that end up here. Explorer › Compliance is the search across all of it.
cta: Name the control — Explorer › Compliance finds every asset that fails it.
